beats.t: Five in the morning. The bakery attic was still dark, and only the borrowing card beneath Yeoni's hoof was warm.
(The First Spring. Not returned. But I've never borrowed a book like that.)
The corner of the card smelled of water. Cold and a little lonely, like the ground at a bus stop after the rain.
Why aren't you asleep? Dawn's still a long way off.
Look. Apparently, there's a book checked out in my name. But I don't remember a thing.
Yeongnyangi looked down at the card. For a fleeting moment, his left paw lifted from the floor, then settled quietly again.
I've heard library overdue fines are terrifying. So go to sleep.
(That paw just now. Is it hurting again? If I ask, he'll just say no again.)
The baby dragon sleeping around Yeoni's wrist woke with a flick of its tail. It sniffed the card, then sneezed loudly onto it.
A bookshelf-sized opening appeared in the attic wall. The sound of turning pages swept through it like breathing.
What now, this early? Pig, what did you open this time? It's not a fridge, is it?
Ah, this door. It's been a while. The Library of Resources.
Mister, you've been here before?
There isn't a sky I haven't visited in three years. This place is quite friendly, as long as you keep quiet.
Quiet. The hardest word in the world for me. Followed by diet.
Beyond the opening, endless bookshelves stretched beneath a domed ceiling. All the books slowly swelled and sank.
The books... they're breathing. They really are.
Every book here is someone's memory. As long as its owner lives and remembers, it breathes like this.
Golden letters slowly rose over the marble floor. The rules of the library.
[ Library of Resources · One book per visitor · A book once read cannot be undone ]
(Exactly one book. Then I only need to find The First Spring. Simple.)
One book? Stingy, stingy. Even a market sample stand lets you come back three times.
Moka's voice echoed to the ceiling. Dozens of books on the nearest shelf snapped their covers shut at once.
Then a papery shhhh spread from all directions. Moka quietly put his ladle between his teeth.
The books are telling you off. Mr. Otter, please keep the rapping to a whisper.
Whispered rap isn't rap. It's prayer. You're asking me to change genres.
Yeongnyangi followed a step behind. Among all the breathing books, he alone seemed to walk holding his breath.
There was no librarian at the central desk. Instead, a large catalog lay open, turning its own pages.
Give it your name, and it'll tell you your shelf. Ladies first.
Yeoni. Oh, and just in case, could you look under Flower Pig, too?
The catalog's letters spread like ink, then gathered into a single line.
[ Flower Pig · Collection: 23 volumes · On loan: 1 volume, The First Spring · Borrower: ■■■ ]
The borrower's name... it's erased. Like someone deliberately blacked it out.
More importantly, twenty-three volumes? Your life's twenty-three books long, pig? Mostly about eating, I bet.
Half of them are reviews! Star ratings are perfectly legitimate memories.
While the others laughed, Yeongnyangi studied the catalog. A tiny bead of water had formed over the erased borrower's name.
Let's find the shelf. This isn't somewhere to linger.
On the way to Yeoni's shelves, Yundal stopped at another section. He pressed his gloved palm hard with his other hand.
Is your book here, too, mister?
It is. Want to see? You need to save your one book, so just the cover.
The book Yundal pulled out was thin. The place for a name on its cover was blank, and its breathing was very shallow.
Every time someone forgets me, it loses a page. Last year, it was twice this thick.
Unable to find an answer, Yeoni stared at the thin book. A fresh line of pencil writing appeared on its last page. The lady called me Yundal.
That was yesterday.
Yes. Thanks to you, I gained a page. It's the first time my book has grown thicker in three years.
Hey, con artist. Save that kind of story for mealtimes. You're giving your listeners indigestion.
Then dinner tonight is on Mr. Otter.
How did you get that from what I said?!
Yeoni's shelf was lower than expected. Every spine bore a tiny flower, and at the far end was a gap the width of one book.
Wow, my books. This is My Elementary School Lunch Ratings. And this is I Hate the Boss at My First Part-Time Job.
Your way of naming things hasn't changed since childhood.
That's a compliment, right? I'll take it as one. No objections accepted.
Yeoni slipped a hoof into the gap. The inside of the shelf was damp. Someone had taken the book with wet hands.
(This is where it was. The First Spring.)
Yeoni. What will you do if you find that book?
Read it. It's my book. Why?
Nothing. Just asking.
Yeongnyangi looked away from the gap. Yeoni was just turning to look at his face again.
Then glass shattered deep in the library. Every breathing book held its breath at once.
In the inner reading room, the most precious memories lay in glass cases. Several black hands crawled over the cases like spiders.
The protected shelves. They only keep memories there that the owner must never forget.
One black hand pierced the glass and picked up a thin book. Then it tore out and ate the pages one by one, savoring them.
[ Mother's Lullaby · Owner: Baby Otter · Pages remaining: 9 → 6 ]
Baby otter? Hey, that belongs to a kid from our island! Spit it out!
Yeongnyangi leaped first. His claws split the black hand, but the severed fingers scattered like ink, then joined again.
I can't cut it. This isn't a body.
A fine read. Other people's memories... always taste so sweet.
The voice came from no single place. It was as though all the darkness between the shelves had opened its mouth at once.
Put that down. It's someone else's lullaby!
Flames burst from Yeoni's hoof. The black hand flinched back, and at the same moment, a nearby bookshelf's corner caught fire.
My lady! This is a library! A library!
Moka beat the burning shelf with his ladle. The books huddled together, rustling like screams.
(No fire. Here, the stronger I get, the more other people's memories burn.)
Yeoni. Breathe first. Set it down on the ground.
Yeoni drew back the fire. Their hoof trembled. The black hand crawled toward the lullaby's remaining pages again.
Then the rules on the floor glowed faintly. Only now did Yeoni see the small writing beneath them.
[ Addendum · A memory read aloud with care returns to its owner ]
(Read it aloud, and it goes back. But that will use up my one book.)
My lady, if you use it now, you won't be able to open The First Spring. One book per person.
I know. But my spring can wait a little. This one's being eaten right now.
Yeoni jumped between the black hands and hugged the lullaby book. The six remaining pages trembled against their chest.
Yeoni read the first page aloud. Sleep well, my baby. The ripples hold you, and Mama holds the ripples.
When the moon rises, the river sleeps, and you sleep, too. Mama is here. When you open your eyes, I'll be here.
The voice was awkward, without a tune. Yet with each line, another black hand slipped from the book.
Care, is it? There's no flavor in that.
As the voice retreated, the black hands dissolved into the darkness. Only Yeoni's reading remained in the room.
At the last page, the book melted into golden light and flew through the ceiling. Toward a sleepless baby otter on some faraway island.
[ Mother's Lullaby · Returned · Reader: Flower Pig (1/1) ]
Pig... you just threw away your one book. You came here to find your twenty-three-volume life.
I didn't throw it away. I lent it. Though I won't ask for it back.
I've never seen a visitor spend their one book on someone else's. If there were a librarian, you'd get a prize.
I'll give the prize. Half my snack tonight.
Half? Only half? Mr. Cat's a little stingy today.
With the black hands gone, the library began breathing again. But something about its breathing sounded damp.
Strange. This sky doesn't even get rain, to protect the paper.
A splash sounded beneath Yeoni's hoof. Cold water seeped up through the cracks in the marble.
A large pawprint marked the puddle. It resembled a cat's, but was several times larger.
The wet tracks circled the reading room and led to the stairs descending below. They smelled like the drop of water on the erased borrower's name.
The tiger. It got here before us.
(The smell of rain. Exactly the same smell as the card.)
Water rose with a rushing sound below the stairs. Then a low, chilling voice floated over it.
I'm taking The First Spring. You can wash away right there, pig.
Water surged upward from the stairs. Every breathing book drew a deep breath at once.
